issues.detail: The Greek 'προσεδεξασθε' (prosedexasthe) is a passive/middle imperative meaning 'receive' or 'accept'. The Vietnamese 'vui lòng chấp nhận' adds the subjective emotion 'vui lòng' (willingly/pleasantly), which is not present in the Greek text.

The Greek 'κρειττονα υπαρξιν' (kreittona hyparxin) refers to a 'better existence' or 'better life/being'. The Vietnamese translation 'của cải tốt hơn' translates this as 'better assets' or 'better wealth', which significantly narrows the scope of the Greek concept.

The Greek 'μενουσαν' (menousan) is a present participle modifying 'υπαρξιν'. The Vietnamese 'còn lại' (remaining) captures the sense of endurance but misses the active/continuous nature of 'abiding' or 'remaining' in the heavenly existence.
